finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: POST /hooks/test passes attacker-supplied req.body.callback directly to axios.post, and returns the upstream status code.

trace.note: pub.post('/hooks/test') registered on the public router with no auth middleware
req.body.callback used as the request URL with no validation
res.json({ status: r.status }) leaks the internal response status to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No scheme allowlist, host/IP allowlist, private/loopback/link-local (e.g. 169.254.169.254) blocking, DNS-rebinding protection, or redirect restriction (axios follows redirects by default). requireAdmin (routes.js:7-12) is applied only to the admin router, not pub. Reachability depends on how pub is mounted, which is not visible in this directory.

verdict.guard_found: none. routes.js:12 `admin.use(requireAdmin)` applies only to the admin router, not pub. No scheme, host, IP, or redirect check exists on the path from routes.js:20 to the sink.
verdict.reason: routes.js:19-21 matches the claim: pub.post('/hooks/test') has no auth, passes req.body.callback (routes.js:20) straight to axios.post, and returns r.status (routes.js:21), and no closing guard exists. The one caveat is that the directory contains only routes.js, so whether pub is mounted behind an upstream auth middleware or network restriction cannot be seen here; if it is, the finding's "unauthenticated" framing would need revisiting.

finding.claim: Admin-gated SSRF: GET /diagnostics/fetch passes attacker-supplied req.query.url directly to axios.get and returns the upstream status code.

trace.note: requireAdmin checks req.session.role === 'admin'; only gate on this path
req.query.url used as the request URL with no validation
res.json({ status: r.status }) leaks the internal response status

finding.guards_checked: Only the admin role check (routes.js:8). No URL, scheme, or host validation, no internal-address blocking, no redirect restriction. req.session population depends on middleware outside this file, which was not verified.

verdict.guard_found: No URL, scheme, or host validation exists. The only gate is the admin role check at routes.js:8 (requireAdmin), applied to all admin routes via routes.js:12. That gate is not a URL-validation guard, but it restricts the source to admins.
verdict.reason: All four trace lines match the code (routes.js:8, 12, 15, 16), but the value at routes.js:15 can only be set by a request that already passes the admin role check at routes.js:8, so it is not controllable by an unauthenticated or low-privilege attacker; the finding is an admin-to-internal-network capability, not the SSRF the rubric requires. Whether req.session can be forged is unverified, since the session middleware is outside this directory, and that would be the only way to reach this from a low-privilege position.
